title: Personal Infinitive: Introduction
summary: Recognize infinitives that show their subject with endings like fazermos and chegarem.

sections.heading: What makes it personal
sections.body: Portuguese infinitives can take subject endings when the infinitive has its own subject. This is called the **infinitivo pessoal**. It is common after prepositions and in more explicit sentences.

examples.en: It is important for us to arrive early.

examples.pt: Antes de vocês saírem, fechem a porta.
examples.en: Before you all leave, close the door.
For them to understand, explain slowly.

sections.heading: Regular endings
sections.body:
The personal infinitive uses the infinitive plus endings: no ending for eu and você/ele/ela, **-mos** for nós, and **-em** for vocês/eles/elas.

| Subject | falar | comer | abrir |
|---|---|---|---|
| eu | **falar** | **comer** | **abrir** |
| você/ele/ela | **falar** | **comer** | **abrir** |
| nós | **falarmos** | **comermos** | **abrirmos** |
| vocês/eles/elas | **falarem** | **comerem** | **abrirem** |

examples.en: After we have lunch, we will go out.
Without them knowing, it becomes difficult.

examples.pt: Por você morar longe, entendo o atraso.
examples.en: Because you live far away, I understand the delay.

sections.heading: When the plain infinitive is enough
sections.body: If the subject is the same as the main verb's subject, Portuguese often uses the plain infinitive. The personal infinitive is most useful when clarity is needed.

examples.en: I want you all to leave early.

examples.pt: É bom estudar todos os dias.
examples.en: It is good to study every day.

keyPoints: Personal infinitive marks the subject of an infinitive.
It is common after prepositions like antes de, depois de, para, por, sem.
Use it when the infinitive has a different or explicit subject.

commonMistakes.note: Nós needs the personal infinitive ending.
Same subject usually uses the plain infinitive.
